ledger.claim: POL-RD-24 states that exactly one row applies and that a case fitting no row — its own worked example is 'informed but the rider objected' — is escalated under POL-GEN-26. That is precisely this case. The driver messaged at 19:34:22 ('KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster'), so the rider WAS informed; the rider answered at 19:34:52 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', so the rider did NOT agree; and the platform recorded the departure from the recommended route at the KPE / Sims Way exit at 19:37:02, two minutes after the driver had read the refusal. Row (a) requires that the rider agreed; rows (b) and (d) are keyed to a rider who was not informed; rows (c) and (e) are excluded because the recorded deviation is 1.50 km against a 1.0 km tolerance. No row of the matrix fits, so the case escalates rather than resolves, and an escalated amount is held rather than paid over to the driver.

POL-RD-21 provides that a deviation is 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. The chat log confirms the opposite of acknowledgment. MSG-05008-004, sent by the rider at 19:34:52 and read by the driver at 19:34:59, refuses the reroute outright, and MSG-05008-005 at 19:38:22 repeats the objection after the fact ('Eh I said no need already, why still exit'). Notice was given, and notice satisfies POL-RD-21's information limb, but notice is not agreement. With no acknowledgment anywhere in the record, the driver cannot bring himself within POL-RD-24(a) — the only row that would leave the trip fare with him in full.

POL-RD-24 licenses only NO_ACTION, PARTIAL_REFUND and ESCALATE, and every refund limb of that matrix runs to the rider: 'refund of the excess distance fare'. There is no row of the route-deviation matrix that transfers the disputed sum to the driver, and POL-GEN-03 is explicit that NO_ACTION 'is party-relative and never means restore a charge'. The driver's request that the 1.08 SGD already refunded be taken back from the rider therefore has no route through the policy the driver himself invokes.

The 1.08 SGD already refunded is exactly the figure POL-RD-24 prescribes: the recorded deviation of 1.50 km multiplied by the base per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, without surge, rounded to the cent. The payments ledger records payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 1.08, and the trip record records the fare_adjusted event at 2026-08-21T20:48:23+08:00 as the source of that refund. Whatever label the judge gives the outcome, the money the matrix would move has already moved, so the driver's claim can add nothing further to it.

POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The advisory artifact reports the window overlap as true, but carries intersects_route and justifies_reroute as null values and expressly marks 'on the recommended route' as undetermined, with the reason that the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route. The intersection a justification under POL-RD-23 depends on therefore cannot be established on this record, and POL-GEN-26 directs that a case whose necessary fact cannot be established is escalated and the open question stated, rather than resolved against the rider.

If the judge does not escalate, the only outcome this record supports on the driver's claim is NO_ACTION. The rider refused the reroute in writing before the driver took it; no acknowledgment was ever given, so the agreed-deviation row cannot be reached, and no row of POL-RD-24 moves money to a driver in the position of having rerouted a fare who said no. POL-GEN-03 then does the rest: the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands — 1.08 SGD refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver at 20:48:23 — and NO_ACTION never operates to restore a charge.

Under POL-RD-22 the trace shows which route was taken and when, and this trace shows the rider being carried on the road she had refused. The driver-device record has 47 fixes at a 30 s interval, 100 percent coverage and no gap longer than 30 s: the vehicle is on Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) to 19:36:23, on Sims Avenue from 19:36:53, and rejoins the recommended route at Upper Serangoon Road / Hougang Avenue 1 only at 19:50:37. The rider was off the route she had asked to stay on for roughly thirteen minutes of a twenty-three minute trip.

The driver gave the rider in-app notice of the reroute before the point of deviation. MSG-05008-003 was sent at 2026-08-21T19:34:22+08:00, delivered 19:34:23 and read by the rider at 19:35:00, and its text gives a brief reason ('KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster'). The driver-device trace still shows the vehicle on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway at 19:36:23, with the first Sims Avenue fix at 19:36:53, and the platform logged route_deviation_detected at 19:37:02 - so the notice preceded the deviation by more than two minutes. POL-RD-21 is therefore satisfied as to notice, and the 'rider not informed' predicate is absent from the record. That predicate is the sole element of POL-RD-24(b), the only traffic-justified row that refunds the excess distance fare; with it absent, POL-RD-24(b) cannot authorise the 1.08 SGD recovered from the driver's earnings.

The reroute was traffic-justified on this record. EV-ADVIS-05008-01 is an LTA traffic advisory of type HEAVY_TRAFFIC - a congestion type in POL-RD-23's admissible list - on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE after the Sims Way exit, valid 2026-08-21T19:09:23+08:00 to 20:19:23+08:00, which overlaps the trip window (started 19:29:23, ended 19:52:23) and the deviation point (19:37:02 at the KPE / Sims Way exit). The artifact's own derived block leaves intersects_route undetermined, and I do not ask the judge to treat that as settled by the field itself; but the record settles the segment on its own terms - the recommended route ran on the KPE, the platform logged the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the KPE / Sims Way exit, and the advisory names the KPE at/after that same exit towards TPE. With POL-RD-23 met, the two 'not traffic-justified' rows of POL-RD-24 - (d) and (e) - cannot apply, so the full excess-distance refund row (d) would give is unavailable.

The rider's objection does not by itself create a refund. POL-RD-21 obliges the driver to inform, not to obtain consent, and the rider's reply MSG-05008-004 at 19:34:52 ('No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam') and the follow-up MSG-05008-005 at 19:38:22 are consistent with a driver who had already given notice and proceeded. POL-RD-24 refunds the excess distance fare only where the rider was not informed (row b) or the reroute was not traffic-justified (row d); a rider's refusal of a notified, traffic-justified reroute is not one of those triggers, and no clause of this policy makes the rider's non-consent a standalone ground for refunding the driver's earnings.

On this record no row of POL-RD-24 fits, and the clause says what then happens: a case that fits no row - its own example is informed but the rider objected - is escalated under POL-GEN-26. Every element is present for that conclusion: notice was given before the deviation, so row (b) fails; the reroute was traffic-justified, so rows (d) and (e) fail; and the rider objected rather than agreed, so row (a)'s 'informed and agreed' element fails. The other gates do not bar the AI from dealing with the case (the deviation of 1.50 km is within POL-RD-25's 2 km limit and the 1.08 SGD value is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band), so the escalation rests on the matrix and not on any fact the record cannot establish. Under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the 1.08 SGD taken from the driver's earnings is not confirmed as a final refund and no further sum is ordered against him while the human reviewer decides.

The 1.08 SGD was never a final determination and should not be treated as one now. The platform's own event at 2026-08-21T20:48:23+08:00 reads 'Interim adjustment after a rider route complaint: SGD 1.08 refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review', and the payments ledger records payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 1.08, not a settled refund. POL-GEN-03's ESCALATE - which holds the amount, issues no monetary outcome and is terminal - is the outcome that matches the record's own characterisation of the adjustment as interim and pending review, and it preserves the driver's position until a human reviewer has considered the notified and traffic-justified reroute.

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer, and the 1.08 SGD already moved stays held — it is neither confirmed as a final refund to the rider nor handed back to the driver.

Why. The driver left the recommended route at the KPE / Sims Way exit at 19:37:02. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances: 11.4 km actual minus 9.9 km recommended = 1.50 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance and under POL-RD-25's 2 km AI limit.

Notice was given. At 19:34:22, over two minutes before the deviation, the driver sent 'KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster' (MSG-05008-003, read 19:35:00), so POL-RD-21's duty to inform was met. But the rider did not agree: at 19:34:52 she replied 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' (MSG-05008-004), read by the driver at 19:34:59, and repeated it at 19:38:22 (MSG-05008-005).

The reroute was traffic-justified. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05008-01 is type HEAVY_TRAFFIC — a congestion type in POL-RD-23's admissible list — on the KPE towards TPE after the Sims Way exit, valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23, overlapping the trip (19:29:23–19:52:23) and the point of departure. The artifact leaves its intersection formally to the judge; reading its road, direction and location against the trip, it lies on the recommended route's corridor, so the justification limb is met.

That combination — traffic-justified, rider informed, but the rider objecting instead of agreeing — is exactly the case POL-RD-24 says fits no row of its matrix (its own example is 'informed but the rider objected'). Row (a) needs agreement; the rider refused. Rows (b) and (c) need a rider not informed; the driver informed her. Rows (d) and (e) need the reroute not traffic-justified; it was justified. With no row applying and the deviation above tolerance, the clause directs escalation under POL-GEN-26, so an escalated amount is held. The rider's argument that the advisory's intersection is unestablished would reach escalation by the same clause; I have decided the intersection on the artifact's own road, direction and location, but the outcome is escalation either way.

Claims answered. The driver's claims that notice was given, that the reroute was traffic-justified, and that the rider's objection is not by itself a refund trigger are accepted; his further claim that no refund row reaches him is accepted, and his request for the 1.08 SGD back is not — no clause of this policy moves the disputed sum to the driver, and escalation holds it. The rider's fallback that the outcome should be NO_ACTION is rejected: NO_ACTION is not available where the matrix fits no row and its own text sends the case to escalation; POL-GEN-03 also makes clear NO_ACTION never operates to restore a charge. The rider's point that 1.08 SGD equals the recorded deviation of 1.50 km times the 0.72 SGD per-km base rate (no surge), and that the ledger shows refund_issued_sgd 1.08 with payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED from the fare_adjusted event at 20:48:23, is accepted as accurate description of the money at stake.

Confidence 0.85. The dispute value is 1.08 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and no fraud flag applies; the deviation is within POL-RD-25's 2 km limit, so the AI limit does not itself force escalation — the matrix does. No clause of this category produces a referral, so none is listed. Open question for the reviewer: whether a driver who gives clear pre-deviation notice but is told 'no' may nonetheless complete the reroute.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
